hints: Think about the big picture first. What are the two major parts of the cell cycle, and which one takes up most of the time?
Remember what happens in the S part of interphase, and think about cells like nerve cells that rarely divide. How long might they stay out of mitosis?
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1 - What is the cell cycle?**

Think of the cell cycle as the whole life of a cell, from one division to the next.

It has two main parts: a long growing and preparing stage called interphase, plus a short dividing stage called mitosis (followed by cytokinesis). So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 - When is DNA copied?**

A cell must double its DNA before it can divide, otherwise the daughter cells would get only half.

This copying, called DNA replication, happens in the S phase of interphase, well before mitosis starts. So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 - How long can interphase last?**

Interphase is very variable. Some cells divide quickly, but others pause in G1 for a very long time.

Specialised cells like nerve cells or muscle cells can stay in interphase (in G0) for months or even years without entering mitosis. So statement 3 is correct.

**Put it together**

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, the answer is A.

options.A: Correct and reassuring. All three statements are true, so 1, 2 and 3 is the right combination.
options.B: Close but incomplete. It correctly includes 1 and 2, but wrongly leaves out 3, as cells can stay in interphase for months.
options.C: Close but incomplete. It correctly includes 1 and 3, but wrongly leaves out 2, as DNA replication does occur in S phase of interphase.
options.D: Close but incomplete. It correctly includes 2 and 3, but wrongly leaves out 1, as the cell cycle is interphase plus mitosis.
